records.title: Learning Task Representations from In-Context Learning
records.reason: The method learns task representations and evaluates task fidelity; it does not reduce prompt tokens or report serving compute/memory/latency. Because it is linked to prompt compression, keep as a weak neighboring lead.

records.title: Hotspot-Driven Peptide Design via Multi-Fragment Autoregressive Extension
records.reason: The peptide-binder pipeline generates amino-acid sequences and evaluates protein binding geometry, so its autoregressive sequence construction is biological design rather than token decoding for an LLM. Its forward citation from multi-token prediction is only a broad autoregression connection; it neither changes model inference nor reports serving resource gains.

records.title: Layer-wise Importance Matters: Less Memory for Better Performance in Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning of Large Language Models
records.reason: Experiments and conclusion show layer-selective reinforcement-learning PEFT reduces fine-tuning memory and compute; it concerns training resources, not inference, and the 70B-scale validation is absent.

records.title: How Do Humans Write Code? Large Models Do It the Same Way Too
records.reason: The paper addresses reasoning correctness and code generation behavior in math tasks through CoT/PoT training and attention/reward strategies. It does not propose a decoding-cost, memory, latency, or serving method; the citation from multi-token prediction does not make its behavioral study an inference-system extension.

records.title: EGA-V2: An End-to-end Generative Framework for Industrial Advertising
records.reason: The generative model jointly handles advertising recommendation, creative selection, allocation, and bidding/payment objectives. Multi-token prediction is used within this application model, but the contribution concerns ad-system decisions and business outcomes rather than LLM decoding or a transferable inference-cost improvement.
